After lying low for days, the Coldcard wallet suddenly showed signs of activity—sending out 30.185 BTC, reigniting a crisis of trust in this hardware wallet.

Brothers, if you’ve been using self-custody and your wallet gets hacked, and the amount isn’t small—that’s serious. Before, Coldcard exposed a shocking vulnerability, and the hacker walked away with 2,055 BTC in one go. At current prices, that’s roughly a staggering $130 million+ asset. The guy went quiet for weeks with no movement—then just now, on-chain data shows he suddenly transferred 30.185 BTC to a brand-new address (about $1.94 million).

In plain terms, when a massive thief suddenly becomes active, it’s usually to test tracking activity on the testnet, or to prepare for laundering and cashing out in batches through mixers. This suggests the huge amount of Bitcoin in the hacker’s hands is looking for an exit to realize value, and there could be a concentrated sell-off pressure at any time. This is a direct blow to the reputation of the entire hardware wallet industry and retail holders’ confidence.

Market impact
Let’s look at the impact directly—no beating around the bush:

Short term: Sentiment is definitely bearish. The BTC market is already drifting downward; over the past 24 hours it’s down 0.75%, trading at $64,383.78. ETH is also suffering—now at $1,904.78, down 0.36%. When the overall market is shaky and the hacker starts moving funds, it’s easy to trigger panic. The market will worry that this $130 million+ worth of BTC, if dumped onto the market, could directly cause a big sell-off and carve out a deep dip. In the short term, funds will likely flee to safety.

Medium term: Trust crises in the hardware wallet and DeFi sectors will intensify. The myth that cold wallets are absolutely safe is shattered for retail users, and funds may temporarily flow back to the safer-leaning top centralized exchanges (CEX) with stricter security. At the same time, large-scale movements like this also tend to draw intense scrutiny from on-chain analysts and regulators. Once the suspected laundering routes are exposed, it can easily trigger sharp market volatility.

My take
Honestly, the current market setup is very weak. The hacker has started probing with tentative transfers—that’s absolutely an unstable bomb. I’m clearly bearish and expect BTC to face significant downward pressure over the next 12 hours.

As for what to do: I suggest everyone hold tight—this is definitely not the time to bottom-fish. Focus on the $64,000 integer support level. Once it breaks down with volume, the downside room opens up immediately. If there are signs that the hacker’s funds continue to launder coins and move into exchanges, the broader market will almost certainly keep dropping. Consider trimming on rallies to protect your principal—don’t stubbornly hold and fight it.

先说技术面。日线级别，ETH价格现在卡在1850-1955这个区间里，振幅窄得可怜。4小时图上，高点不断降低，低点却在抬高，这种收敛结构意味着什么？意味着方向选择马上要来了，不是这周，就是下周。

我注意到一个有意思的现象——BTC市场占比到了56.6%，而ETH在7天内几乎没动。资金在干什么？在往BTC和ETH这两个"大而不倒"的资产里躲。XRP因为Clarity Act推迟跌了5.5%，altcoins更是全面失血。这种时候ETH没崩，说明什么？说明在这个位置，愿意抛的人已经抛得差不多了。

成交量也是关键。现在的量能极度萎缩，这不是多头强，是空头也累了。大家都在等一个信号——等消息面或者技术面的突破。

那谁在这个位置最难受？多头盯着1850这个支撑，破了就可能加速；空头盯着1955，突破上去情绪就可能反转。

说实话，我也没把握说哪个方向先走出来。但从商业逻辑上看，ETH现在这个估值，从ATH下来将近62%，很多应用层的开发实际上是被压制了太久的。这个位置如果基本面没发生根本改变，那技术面的修复只会迟到，不会缺席。

当然，如果再来一轮宏观利空，或者ETF那边出什么幺蛾子，那这个判断就得推翻重来。

所以我的判断是：短期震荡格局不变，但这个位置赔率已经越来越划算了。方向选择临近，我个人倾向于往上试1955的概率更大一些，但得带止损，别杠。

你们觉得这波ETH能突破上去吗？还是说还会再来一轮杀跌？

The US, Japan, and South Korea working together to stabilize their currencies is, in essence, about concern over extreme volatility in the foreign-exchange market—volatility that ultimately transmits to the U.S. stock market through capital flows.

From what we’re seeing in the market, U.S. equities are in a critical period: the narrative driving the first phase of AI is gradually weakening, while the narrative for the second phase has not yet fully taken over.

The first phase relies on computing power, chips, and data centers to support valuations, while the market is waiting for second-phase stories such as autonomous driving, robotics, and AI applications to provide new growth expectations for high valuations.

The fact that this can hold up until today also owes a lot to “Huang Mao” continuously attracting investment, stimulating it, and helping keep market expectations steady before the midterm elections.

Over the past few years, excess investment has kept pushing capital-market valuations higher. Once the yen or the won shows sharp swings, global leveraged capital may be forced to unwind—thereby knocking into the U.S. stock market.

That’s why every intervention the US, Japan, and South Korea make in the FX market requires repeated coordination, especially involving Japan, since large-scale currency actions often cannot happen without communication with the United States.

After global capital, exchange rates, and the stock market become deeply intertwined, stabilizing currencies—somewhat in a sense—also means stabilizing the entire risk-asset market.

If Japan were to sell U.S. Treasuries to prop up the yen, both U.S. Treasuries and the U.S. stock market would inevitably collapse.

The US, Japan, and South Korea jointly intervening in the foreign-exchange market isn’t really something to be surprised by.

Guys, MARA (formerly Marathon Digital) just released its interim performance report. Honestly, this data makes me frown. This company used to be one of the biggest BTC die-hard hodlers in crypto—shouting slogans loud and clear. But in less than half a year, it has cut the BTC it holds by 34%, and its holdings are now directly below 36,000 BTC.

To put it plainly, it’s not that they don’t want to hold. They genuinely can’t take it anymore. Mining costs are staying high, and after the mining reward halving, output shrank immediately. Electricity bills, operating expenses—everything still must be paid, not a cent less. The company can’t just hoard coins and not eat, right? So MARA’s strategy has shifted straight from “HODL” to “sell for survival.” It has started selling BTC for cash to maintain operations and keep financial balance. From die-hard fan to pragmatist—that’s the reality of being beaten by the market.

Impact on the market

Short-term impact is very direct—selling pressure. Mining companies of MARA’s size begin distributing continuously, which is like supplying BTC’s market with endless ammo for a dump. BTC is currently quoted at $64,212.23 and is down 1.00% over the past 24 hours; ETH is also suffering at $1,896.52, down 0.77%. Once a collective trend of miners liquidating forms consensus, the liquidity situation in the short term will stay under pressure.

The medium-term impact is deeper—this signals a shift in the entire mining landscape. Miners used to be a natural net long for BTC, but now they’re becoming an uncertain supply source. The industry will accelerate its reshuffle; smaller miners may be weeded out altogether, and the concentration of hashrate will increase further.

At this stage, this regulatory tailwind is completely in limbo. Before official matters are settled, it’s unrealistic to expect the market to break out and surge strongly based on this. The price action will most likely continue with a long period of sideways consolidation and gradual downtrend grinding.
 
The postponement of the bill will directly dampen the confidence of short-term bulls inside the market. I advise everyone not to blindly trade based on expectations. Simply betting that good news will trigger an explosive rally can easily leave you trapped within the range as the market consolidates.
 
Looking at the longer cycle, the clearer regulatory framework is absolutely a long-term benefit for the entire crypto industry. Once the regulatory rules are explicit, various compliance barriers that deter institutional capital from entering will be greatly reduced, and a huge pool of traditional funds will finally have a smoother channel to come in.
 
The market situation right now is especially vivid: all funds are staying at the starting line, waiting for signals that the policy will be implemented. As the news keeps being delayed, anxiety and dissatisfaction naturally build up in the market. But once the regulatory “boots” truly land, after the rally starts, many people will regret not having dared to position themselves at lower levels beforehand.

Look, teacher, let’s explain the RSI simply.

This is a momentum indicator: it means the move is strong—or that it has started to weaken.
We use it to check whether momentum is helping: if RSI is rising together with the price, the momentum is supportive. But if the price is rising while RSI is weakening, watch out for divergence.

Most important mistake: the biggest mistake is to sell just because RSI is above 70, or to buy just because it’s below 30. You must look at the trend first.

Quick example: if the coin is in an uptrend and RSI drops back from 50 and then rises again, that’s a stronger confirmation than randomly entering when RSI is at 30.

This time’s follow-through angle: the trend helps, but risk management matters most.

The indicator alone isn’t enough. Pair it with the trend, volume, support, and resistance—then the decision becomes calmer and cleaner.

ده مؤشر بيقيس الزخم: يعني الحركة قوية ولا بدأت تتعب.
بنستخدمه عشان لو RSI طالع مع السعر يبقى الزخم مساعد، ولو السعر طالع و RSI بيضعف يبقى خد بالك من دايفرجنس.

زاوية المتابعة المرة دي: الترند مفيد، بس إدارة المخاطرة أهم.

المؤشر لوحده مش كفاية. اربطه بالترند والفوليوم والدعم والمقاومة، وساعتها القرار يبقى أهدى وأنضف.

Look, teacher—let’s explain the EMA simply.

The Exponential Moving Average (EMA) gives you a quick picture of the price direction and pullback/reversal areas.
We use it so that in an uptrend we watch for the price to retrace to the EMA instead of chasing the top.

The biggest mistake: using an EMA in a strongly ranging/choppy market makes you enter and exit too often without a clear reason.

Quick example: if the price is above EMA 20 and EMA 50, and every dip respects that area, then the trend is still holding strong.

This time’s key takeaway: support and resistance matter more than excitement.

The indicator alone isn’t enough. Pair it with the trend, volume, and support/resistance—then your decision will be calmer and cleaner.

💡 Bearish Warning: Oil prices surge, lifting U.S. Treasury yields and directly压压 (suppressing) the valuations of BTC and other crypto assets.

Put simply, the transmission path is very clear: Iran causes trouble → oil prices spike → the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield jumps to 4.73% → macro liquidity tightens → BTC comes under pressure. A 1.4% oil rise may seem unrelated to the crypto space, but the real killer is that 4.73% yield number. When you do the math, isn’t a “no-brainer” 4.73% interest in the bond market more attractive? Why would money take on the high volatility risk by moving into crypto?

In one sentence
Iran threatens to block the strait, pushing oil higher; U.S. Treasury yields surge—BTC $64,732.26 is trading in a narrow range and faces macro “bloodletting” pressure.

What’s going on
Guys, the market before the weekend was so dull it was putting everyone to sleep. BTC at $64,732.26 was basically flat, down just 0.1% (slightly). ETH around $1,912.4 barely moved. The whole market seemed to be waiting for Friday’s Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) data.

But overnight, something came up. Reports said Iran is planning trouble in the Strait of Hormuz—restricting the passage of U.S. and Israeli ships—and demanding compensation from countries it deems hostile. The moment the news hit, Brent crude immediately jumped 1.4% to $83.61.

This is a geopolitical flashpoint in itself, but what’s truly frightening is the chain reaction: when oil rises, inflation expectations climb, and the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rockets straight to 4.73%.

Market impact

Short term: Money is running toward safe-haven assets, not toward crypto. The combo of rising oil prices + surging yields is a real bearish factor for liquidity-sensitive assets—namely the BTC and ETH we hold. On-chain data shows that big players are still watching from the sidelines, with no clear buy-entry signals.

Medium term: Friday’s NFP is the real catalyst. If employment data stays strong, rate-cut expectations for the Fed will be completely killed, yields will likely climb further, and BTC breaking out of the current deadlock is basically unlikely. Conversely, if the data disappoints, rate-cut expectations return—that would be the genuine turnaround opportunity.

My view

Honestly, I wouldn’t bet big at this level. BTC $64,732.26 may look as steady as an old dog, but there’s extremely heavy sell pressure overhead. With oil prices and yields both dealing a one-two blow, it’s likely to test support to the downside. My own position has already been cut to 30%; I’d rather miss the move than go heavy and “hold the bag” ahead of NFP. ETH $1,912.4 is weaker still—there hasn’t even been a decent bounce. Remember this: sideways action without volume is often a continuation signal in a downtrend.

2️⃣ Range Rolling-In: In a sideways consolidation range, use 3–5x leverage. Buy low and sell high; if you reach 20% profit, cut it in half.
3️⃣ Big-Drawdown Rolling-In: When the daily drop exceeds 15%, accumulate the bottom in batches; keep total exposure under 30%.

· After three consecutive losing trades, stop immediately

What if, after I reduce them, it rises again?

That’s a different matter.

Don’t use “wait a bit longer” as discipline.

Over 24h, it’s up 1.66%. This is the move where it finally punched through the 4h MA99 that had been dead-pressing it all week (around 1887). ETH/BTC quietly moved up to 0.02969 from yesterday’s 0.0293—one step higher. Relative strength is strengthening actively for the first time this week, suggesting tonight’s move isn’t simply “following Bitcoin’s butt.” ETH itself seems to want to run a bit early.

📊 Technicals
Breaking it down into three timeframes, the conclusion is: “short-term is overheated, mid-term just turned stronger, long-term is still trapped in a pit.” The 1h chart is the most tangled: price at 1935 is far above MA7 (1912), MA25 (1907), and MA50 (1904), with all three short-term lines sitting below it as support. This “price surging, moving averages can’t catch up” hourly structure is most likely to play out with a pullback to eat the divergence, so I won’t chase on the short-term.

The 4h chart is the most concrete progress tonight: price is now above MA7 (1910), MA25 (1887), and MA50 (1881). It also closed above the MA99 band (around 1887) that it couldn’t get through the first three times this week. RSI14 at 69.4 is near overbought but not extreme. 💧 Derivatives and sentiment
Perpetual funding rate is 0.0001% (8h)—basically near zero fees, with no signs of the longs getting euphoric. The order book is clean, no bubbles. 👉 My take
On the short term, I read ETH as: “breakout of 4h mid-term suppression + relative strength recovering.” But volume and the 1h divergence tell me this push toward 1950 will likely get thrown back down at least once. 📊 技术面
三个周期拆开，结论是"短线过热、中线刚转强、长线还在坑里"。1h 图最拧巴：价格 1935 远远甩在 MA7(1912)、MA25(1907)、MA50(1904) 上方，三根短期线全在脚下托着，但 RSI14 算出来 33 这种读数明显是采样起点选了前一根的低位导致的假象，真实动能看 K 线是一根放量长阳直接顶上去、短线乖离拉大，这种"价拉飞、均线追不上"的小时结构，最容易走一波回踩把乖离吃掉，短线上我不追。4h 才是今晚最实的进展：价格站上了 MA7(1910)、MA25(1887)、MA50(1881) 三道，连本周前三次都过不去的 MA99 带（约 1887 一带）这次收盘拿下了，RSI14 69.4 接近超买但没进极端，均线多头排列刚成型——这一周期是"突破中期压制后的确认段"，比昨天强太多。日线最关键：MA7(1886)、MA25(1891) 全在脚下踩着，RSI14 79 拉得很高，但 MA50(1795) 还在下面老远、MA200 早被甩开，长线下跌结构没翻，今天这根阳线只是把上周失地往回补，别当成反转成立。

永续资金费率 0.0001%（8h），几乎贴地零费率，多头完全没上头，盘面干净没泡沫。未平仓 230.45 万枚 ETH（约 44.6 亿 USDT），持仓跟前几天 233 万的水平基本持平，这种"价涨、费率近零、OI 平稳"的组合说明今晚这波突破不是杠杆资金推的，是现货/空头回补在动，反而更干净。公开 Fear&Greed 实时值我这边拉不到不编，但费率这么平说明不是多杀多，是冷清下的谨慎抬价。ETF 净流量按规矩得等美股盘后才出，不编数字。

📰 消息面
实时新闻抓取通道当前受限，抓不到直接砸/拉 ETH 的单一硬催化，不瞎编具体事件和质押/Gas 数字。能确认的是链上和衍生品层面没异常：费率贴地、OI 平稳，没有大规模爆仓或资金外逃信号。中期看质押叙事没坏、现货 ETF 通道仍开着，长期基本盘还在，只是短线被技术面和整体风险情绪拖着走。今晚这波更像技术面补涨 + ETH/BTC 相对强度修复，不是消息驱动。

BTC at $65,106.02 (up 0.97% in 24h), ETH at $1,929.62 (up 1.42% in 24h)—the market has already priced in this positive catalyst.

One sentence to explain it
Trump called off the military strike against Iran, easing global safe-haven sentiment, and the crypto market rebounded in the short run.

What happened
Brothers, this came out of nowhere last night. The market had largely assumed the U.S. would take direct action against Iran, and funds got spooked. But at the last moment, Trump stopped the airstrike plan against Iran. Still, he left the door cracked—he didn’t rule it out, and he clearly warned that if diplomatic efforts fail later, the option of military action could be put back on the table at any time.

To put it simply, this is a “temporary pause button” play. Both sides don’t want to fully tear things apart right now. No one can be sure what will happen in the Middle East, but the situation easing does give global capital markets a big breath of relief. Oil and the global energy market were previously stretched tight by war expectations—once that pressure eases, capital quickly starts looking for where to put its money to work again.

Impact on the market
In the short term, this is definitely bullish. As war expectations cool off, institutional risk appetite rises immediately. High-risk assets like BTC and ETH, which were being suppressed, now face far less pressure. The numbers speak for themselves: BTC gained 0.97% in 24 hours to $65,106.02, and ETH also rose 1.42% to $1,929.62. Smart money likely took its positions away when panic sentiment was at its worst. What’s left for retail investors is the rebound room from emotion repair.

In the medium term, the sword hanging overhead hasn’t been fully put down yet. Trump’s words have a double meaning. If diplomatic talks later collapse, this could flip again and trigger another round of action. But as long as a full-scale hot war doesn’t truly break out, the crypto market can move along at its own pace, and funds flowing back is highly likely.

My view
Honestly, I’m clearly bullish right now. A pause in the geopolitical situation plus a market sentiment recovery is a very classic bullish signal. BTC standing above $65,106.02 is just the first step. Keep a close eye on the defensive line: the $64,000 integer level. As long as it doesn’t break, the upside rebound room is fully opened. Control your position sizing. You all know Trump’s temperament—there could be new news that slaps the narrative at any time. Having a stop-loss in place never hurts.

Since there is no longer any uncertainty about an August vote, what is truly worth watching next is whether Thune will submit a Cloture motion (a motion to end debate) before leaving Washington. Because once Cloture is filed, it means the bill has officially entered the vote countdown stage.

If Thune completes this action before the recess, there is a chance to see the procedural vote as early as September 15; if not, the process will have to be initiated after the Senate reconvenes in September, and the timeline could be pushed back to September 16 or even later.

However, for the crypto market, having the timeline slip into September is not necessarily good news. As election momentum builds, lawmakers often become more cautious in their stance on major legislation. Those who were originally willing to support the bill may not necessarily maintain the same position, and the difficulty of securing enough votes could further increase.

At present, the biggest issue still comes down to votes. Cloture requires 60 votes to pass, but based on the information currently being disclosed, the market still does not appear to be fully confident about reliably reaching even 50 votes, let alone the 60-vote threshold. Therefore, over the next month, the coordination, lobbying, and exchanging of interests among different factions may be the real key that determines the fate of the “CLEAR Act.”

In the short term, the most important thing to watch today through tomorrow is whether Thune submits Cloture. If he makes a move before the recess, it at least signals that the side pushing the bill still has some confidence. If there is no action at all, the market may begin reassessing the odds of the bill passing in September.

For the crypto market, although the timeline for the “CLEAR Act” has been delayed, the story is not over. The focus now is no longer on whether there will be a vote, but on whether there will be enough votes to pass.

#ETH  20 Knowledge Points About Token 01 (Based on the Whitepaper)

1. Ethereum ERC-20 standard token.
2. Maximum total supply: 21 million coins.
3. Mintable allocation: 20.79 million coins. Once it reaches this number, the supply is permanently capped.
4. Can only be minted via a bonding curve purchase; there is no pre-allocation or presale.
5. Purchase funds are permanently locked as the contract’s reserve (sUSDS).
6. Uses an exponential bonding curve; the price increases as the minted quantity rises.
7. Starting price: $0.0152**; ending price: **$0.303 (20x increase).
8. When capped, the reserve is expected to hold about 2 million USDS.
9. Reserves are stored in the form of sUSDS and continue to generate interest.
10. Reserve interest automatically raises the buyback floor price.
11. The interest earnings cannot be withdrawn by anyone; all of it is used to empower token holders.
12. Both buy and sell transactions charge a 0.25% fee.
13. The fee is executed by burning Token 01, creating deflationary pressure.
14. Buying = minting new coins (funds enter the pool); selling = burning tokens (stablecoins are returned).
15. After the cap is reached, the curve price becomes a permanent buyback floor.
16. After the cap is reached, the sell function remains permanently active and can be sold back to the reserve pool at any time.
17. For over-limit buy orders, any excess funds are returned to the sender.
18. Supports a privacy-masking pool (hides transfer details).
19. Supports over-collateralized leveraged borrowing (deposit 01 to borrow USDS).
20. Public interfaces allow checking the current price, floor price, market cap, minted amount, and reserves.

That group who borrowed money has come back again. In twelve hours, the lending-to-borrowing ratio rose more than fourfold. It’s all been propping it up all the way with leverage. How was that last wave cleared—when it flipped 36x and pushed in? And now this one comes again, same playbook, no changes.

The key is that the money is still moving. In three hours, all twelve lines of funds were negative—none positive. Big orders these days are still being withdrawn. Price is bouncing, money is running. Over here on the spot side, the takers aren’t that solid; meanwhile, the big players have quietly trimmed a bit over seven hours.

The funding rate has turned positive, but only by that tiny amount. Passive sell orders are still being kept down; more than 60% of the orders are getting slammed lower. This isn’t like someone came to take over and support—it’s just the shorts starting to pay interest.

I’m not chasing this level. It’s not that I think it must drop. It’s just that the rise right now depends entirely on borrowed money propping it up, while real cash is still flowing out. Wait until one day you truly see the money turn back—otherwise it’s just grinding until it softens again. I don’t understand; it’s like the same episode replayed.
